PORTFOLIO HEALTH — HONEST ASSESSMENT: The headline number here is hard to ignore: 0% win rate across 13 completed trades, average loss -4.78%. The Sortino ratio of -15.79 signals the account is taking asymmetric downside risk without compensating upside. Max drawdown is 9.3% on a paper account that should be focused on capital preservation first. This pattern demands restraint, not more activity.

EXISTING POSITION REVIEW:
• AMP (-10.01%, $9,355): AMP does NOT appear in today's screened candidate list — meaning it likely failed the trend filter, consistent with the -10% loss. This position has been stopped out twice before in the trade journal (both losses). The thesis appears broken. While I cannot formally propose a SELL in the JSON schema (not in candidate list), this position should be reviewed for exit outside this system — a third consecutive loss in the same name is a strong signal the original thesis was wrong.
• FOXA (-1.67%, $11,517): Also absent from the screened list. Minor loss but bears watching; if the trend has deteriorated it does not meet entry criteria today.
• MCO (-3.61%, $11,807): Also absent from the screened list. Moderate loss; same monitoring note as FOXA.
• IT (+1.08%, $8,581): IN the screened list — uptrend basing, 46% of 52w range, PEG 0.74, fwd P/E 11.4. Thesis intact; hold.
• NVDA (+5.46%, $16,118): IN the screened list — uptrend, fwd P/E 14.56, PEG 0.48, FCF $41.8B. Thesis intact; hold. Position is at 90% of 52w range so do not add.

NEW TRADE DECISION — ZERO NEW POSITIONS THIS CYCLE:
We are already at the 5-position ceiling defined by the strategy. Three of those five positions are losers, two of which (AMP, MCO, FOXA) are absent from the screened list. Deploying the remaining $31,866 headroom into a sixth name when the existing book is underperforming would compound concentration risk, not reduce it. The best setups on the screened list (ULTA at 37% range, TEL at 32%, HCA at 37%) are all entering earnings within 20-30 days, which creates binary event risk inconsistent with a position-sizing approach that relies on orderly stop-loss exits. CRM and PLTR are fundamentally interesting but at 70-80% of their 52w range — not the Stage 1→2 basing entries this strategy targets. The honest, evidence-based action this cycle is to hold cash, monitor AMP/FOXA/MCO for manual exits, and let IT and NVDA run with their existing stops. Cash at ~39% of equity is not a failure — it is the correct risk-adjusted posture given the win-rate record and proximity of earnings catalysts across the candidate universe.
